title: Thousands march in Barcelona for housing relief, clashes with police reported

tea.why: Protesters are responding to Spain's housing crisis and the government's legislative defeat on emergency housing measures.
tea.want: Protesters demand government action and relief measures to address the housing crisis.
tea.changed: Oct 5: Clashes between protesters and police resulted in injuries and arrests after the demonstration.

summary: Tens of thousands of people marched in Barcelona on October 5, 2026, to protest Spain's housing crisis. The demonstration, organized by the Tenants' Union of Catalonia, began in Urquinaona Square. Protesters demanded housing relief measures after the government's emergency housing proposals were defeated in parliament. After the official protest ended, clashes occurred between demonstrators and police near the city's stock exchange. During the confrontations, some protesters threw objects and set bins on fire, while police retaliated. Police reported approximately 20,000 participants, while organizers claimed around 120,000 people attended. Nearly 30 officers were injured, and 13 individuals were arrested during the unrest.
response: Police blocked demonstrators from advancing, leading to clashes where officers retaliated against thrown objects and fires. The government's emergency housing measures were defeated in parliament by right-wing parties.

crowd.text: Around 120,000 people flooded the streets to demand measures against the housing crisis according to the organisers…

arrests.text: 13 people including a minor were arrested in the clashes last night in the Catalan capital’s city centre.
